2027-02-15.title: Monday of the second week of the Great Fast
readings: The sign of the covenant in the flesh
Devote yourselves to prayer; let your speech be gracious
Do not worry; strive first for the kingdom
2027-02-15.alt: Great Fast (Valiya Nombu), second week. Anniversary of the episcopal ordination of Mathews Mar Pachomios (2024).
2027-02-15.verse: But strive first for the kingdom of God and his righteousness, and all these things will be given to you as well.
theo: The second week of the Fast opens with a hard sign. God tells Abraham: “This is my covenant, which you shall keep, between me and you and your offspring after you: Every male among you shall be circumcised… and it shall be a sign of the covenant between me and you.” The covenant was not only an idea in Abraham's head; it was cut into the body of every man in his household, from the eight-day-old child to the slave bought with money. God wanted his people to carry his promise in their own flesh. Moses would later say what the sign pointed to: “the Lord your God will circumcise your heart.” And Paul tells the Colossians that in Christ they “were circumcised with a spiritual circumcision”, in baptism. The Fast is the time to let God finish that work: to cut away from the heart what does not belong to the covenant.

Paul shows what a marked life looks like in ordinary days: “Devote yourselves to prayer, keeping alert in it with thanksgiving… Conduct yourselves wisely toward outsiders, making the most of the time. Let your speech always be gracious, seasoned with salt.” A fast that sours our speech has missed its point. And Jesus takes away the worry that eats at a fasting heart: “do not worry about your life, what you will eat or what you will drink… Look at the birds of the air… Consider the lilies of the field.” We give up some food in Lent partly to learn this: that “your heavenly Father knows that you need all these things.” So “strive first for the kingdom of God and his righteousness, and all these things will be given to you as well.” St John Chrysostom says that Jesus does not forbid work, only anxiety; he wants us to sow and labour while trusting the Father who feeds the birds (in substance). Today we also pray for Mathews Mar Pachomios on the anniversary of his episcopal ordination.
outline: Ask: what do you carry on your body that shows whom you belong to?
Point 1 · A sign in the flesh
The covenant cut into Abraham's household.
Point 3 · Strive first for the kingdom
The birds, the lilies and the Father who knows.
“Strive first for the kingdom of God and his righteousness.”
live: For one day, before you speak in anger or complaint, count to five and choose a gracious word.
Write down the worry that most troubles you this week, place it before the Lord in prayer, and do today's work without carrying tomorrow's.
2027-02-15.prayer: Heavenly Father, you made a covenant with Abraham and marked his people as your own. Circumcise our hearts in this Fast, and cut away whatever keeps us from loving you. Teach us to pray with thanksgiving, to speak with grace, and to seek first your kingdom, trusting that you know all we need. Bless Mathews Mar Pachomios and all the shepherds of your Church. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.
altar: At the altar we receive the sign of the new covenant, not cut into our flesh but given in the Body and Blood of Christ.

quick: God gave Abraham circumcision as the sign of his covenant.
Paul asks for steady prayer and speech seasoned with salt.
Jesus says: do not worry; strive first for the kingdom of God.
2027-02-15.action: Before any harsh word today, pause and choose a gracious one.
2027-02-15.question: What worry do I carry that the Father already knows about?

family.explain: Jesus told us to look at the birds and the flowers. Birds do not have kitchens or shops, but God feeds them. Flowers do not sew clothes, but God makes them beautiful. If God cares for them, he cares for us much more.
family.intention: We pray for families who are worried about food, money or work.
family.ask: Ask: “What is one worry we can give to God together tonight?”

illus: A fish seller in Neendakara used to wake at three every morning with her stomach knotted: would the boats come in, would the price be fair, would there be enough for school fees? One Lent her parish priest suggested she say one sentence before she left the house: Father, you know what we need today. She said it grudgingly at first. The boats did not come in more often. But she noticed that she stopped snapping at her children over breakfast, and that she had begun to sing on the way to the harbour.

pm.open: Father in heaven, you know what we need before we ask. Take our worries and give us your kingdom. Amen.
share: So shall my covenant be in your flesh (Genesis 17:13). What in my daily life shows that I belong to God?
Let your speech always be gracious, seasoned with salt (Colossians 4:6). How did my words taste to others this past week?
Do not worry about tomorrow (Matthew 6:34). What tomorrow am I carrying today?
pm.resp: Father, we seek first your kingdom.
interc: For Mathews Mar Pachomios on the anniversary of his ordination, and for all our bishops.
For those who are anxious about money, food or work.
For fishermen, farmers and all who depend on weather and harvest.
For those whose words have wounded others, and for those they wounded.
For catechumens and all preparing for baptism this Easter.
pm.close: Father, you feed the birds and clothe the lilies. Free us from anxiety, season our speech with grace, and keep us faithful to the covenant sealed in the blood of your Son. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

homily: Dear friends, God told Abraham to mark every man in his household with the sign of the covenant: so shall my covenant be in your flesh an everlasting covenant (Genesis 17:13). God's promise was meant to be carried in the body, not only in the mind.

In Christ the sign is deeper. Moses foretold it: the Lord your God will circumcise your heart (Deuteronomy 30:6). In baptism we were marked for God, and in the Fast we let him cut away what still does not belong to him.

Paul shows us the marks of a covenant life: devote yourselves to prayer, keeping alert in it with thanksgiving; let your speech always be gracious, seasoned with salt (Colossians 4:2, 6). Fasting that makes us irritable has not yet reached the heart.

And Jesus says: do not worry. Look at the birds of the air; consider the lilies of the field. Strive first for the kingdom of God and his righteousness, and all these things will be given to you as well (Matthew 6:26, 28, 33). Let us give our worries to the Father this week and pray for Mathews Mar Pachomios. Amen.
kids: Children, Jesus said: look at the birds! They do not go shopping, but God feeds them. Look at the flowers! They do not sew clothes, but God makes them beautiful. God loves you much more than birds and flowers, so you do not need to be afraid. Tell God your worries tonight.

intro: Theme: “Strive first for the kingdom of God and his righteousness.”
A covenant marked in the body, a life seasoned with salt, a heart set free from worry.

sub: Every male, from eight days old.
Circumcision of the heart in baptism.
q: Moreover, the Lord your God will circumcise your heart and the heart of your descendants, so that you will love the Lord your God with all your heart and with all your soul, in order that you may live.
In him also you were circumcised with a spiritual circumcision, by putting off the body of the flesh in the circumcision of Christ;
points.apply: Renew your baptismal promises quietly each morning this week.

q: A soft answer turns away wrath, but a harsh word stirs up anger.
Let your speech always be gracious, seasoned with salt, so that you may know how you ought to answer everyone.
points.apply: Fast from one habit of harsh or complaining speech for the rest of the week.

sub: Today's trouble is enough for today.
q: Cast your burden on the Lord, and he will sustain you; he will never permit the righteous to be moved.
Cast all your anxiety on him, because he cares for you.
points.apply: Each night this week, name one worry and hand it to the Father before sleep.

concl: The covenant is cut into the heart, not only the body.
Those who seek the kingdom first are freed from the tyranny of worry.
2027-02-15.resolve: Each day of this week, pray before anything else: Father, your kingdom first.
